outline.chapter_title: Mathematical Reasoning with LLMs: Why DeepSeekMath Matters
outline.description: Introduce the challenge of mathematical reasoning for language models, the motivation behind DeepSeekMath, and its headline results relative to state-of-the-art systems.
subtopics: Why math is hard for LLMs: structure, precision, multi-step dependencies
Closed vs open models: the accessibility gap (GPT-4, Gemini-Ultra vs open-source)
DeepSeekMath at a glance: 7B parameters, 120B math tokens, 51.7% on MATH without tools or voting
Self-consistency improvements: 60.9% on MATH with 64 samples
Key ingredients: large-scale web-mined math corpus and GRPO reinforcement learning
Contributions overview: scalable pretraining, multilingual math, efficient RL, unified training paradigm

outline.chapter_title: Evaluation Landscape and Metrics for Reasoning Models
outline.description: Survey the benchmarks, tasks, and metrics used to evaluate mathematical and general reasoning, code generation, and formal mathematics.
subtopics: Benchmarks for English math: GSM8K, MATH, SAT, OCW Courses, MMLU-STEM
Chinese math benchmarks: MGSM-zh, CMATH, Gaokao-MathCloze, Gaokao-MathQA
General reasoning and coding: BBH, HumanEval, MBPP
Formal mathematics: miniF2F with Isabelle
Evaluation settings: no-tool (pure text) vs tool-integrated (Python, sympy)
Metrics: exact answer accuracy, few-shot vs zero-shot, self-consistency voting, Pass@K and Maj@K
Contamination concerns and decontamination protocols

outline.chapter_title: From the Web to a Math Corpus: Building DeepSeekMath
outline.description: Detail the iterative pipeline for mining high-quality mathematical text from Common Crawl using a fastText classifier and human-in-the-loop refinement.
subtopics: Starting from a seed: OpenWebMath as positive examples
Training the fastText classifier: hyperparameters and negatives from CC
Crawl preprocessing: URL deduplication and near-deduplication at web scale
High-score harvesting: selecting top-ranked math pages by classifier score
Domain mining: identifying math-heavy domains and annotating math-specific URL paths
Iterative bootstrapping across four rounds to 35.5M pages and 120B tokens
Multilingual focus: English and Chinese prominence
Data volume selection via pretraining trials at 40B, 80B, 120B, 160B tokens
Decontamination rules: 10-gram exact match and handling short sequences

outline.chapter_title: Validating Corpus Quality: Comparative Pretraining Experiments
outline.description: Compare the DeepSeekMath Corpus to MathPile, OpenWebMath, and Proof-Pile-2 through controlled pretraining on a 1.3B model and standardized training schedules.
subtopics: Experimental setup: DeepSeek-LLM 1.3B, 150B training tokens per corpus
Optimizer, schedule, and batch settings (AdamW, multistep LR, 4M tokens, 4K context)
Baselines: MathPile (8.9B, arXiv-heavy), OpenWebMath (13.6B), Proof-Pile-2 (with arXiv, web, code)
Quality findings: stronger downstream results with DeepSeekMath at fewer epochs
Scaling behavior: steeper learning curves and fewer repeats before plateau
Multilingual benefits: improved Chinese reasoning vs English-only corpora
Takeaway: web-mined math at scale can surpass arXiv-heavy designs

outline.chapter_title: Training DeepSeekMath-Base 7B: Data Mixtures and Generalization
outline.description: Explain how DeepSeekMath-Base 7B was initialized, trained, and evaluated across math, tool-use, formal math, and general reasoning tasks.
subtopics: Starting point: DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B
Training distribution: 56% DeepSeekMath Corpus, 4% AlgebraicStack, 10% arXiv, 20% GitHub code, 10% general English/Chinese
Training schedule: 500B tokens, LR and batch details
CoT reasoning results: outperforming Mistral 7B and Llemma 34B; exceeding Minerva 540B on MATH
Program-of-Thought results: stronger Python-based solving on GSM8K, MATH
Formal mathematics: few-shot autoformalization on miniF2F with Isabelle and Sledgehammer integration
General benchmarks: boosts on MMLU and BBH; preserved coding on HumanEval and MBPP
Implication: math pretraining improves broad reasoning, not just math

outline.chapter_title: Reasoning Modalities: Chain-of-Thought, Program-of-Thought, and Tools
outline.description: Teach the reasoning paradigms used in DeepSeekMath, how they are prompted, and when to favor each.
subtopics: Chain-of-Thought (CoT): step-by-step natural language reasoning
Program-of-Thought (PoT): using code to compute and verify intermediate steps
Tool-integrated reasoning: Python environment, math and sympy libraries
Prompting strategies and examples
Failure modes and error analysis across modalities
When tools help: arithmetic precision, algebraic manipulation, and symbolic math

outline.chapter_title: Supervised Fine-Tuning for Math: Data and Protocol
outline.description: Describe the 776K-example instruction-tuning set across English and Chinese, training details, and performance of DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B.
subtopics: English sources: GSM8K, MATH (tool-integrated annotations), MathInstruct subset, Lila-OOD training set
Chinese K-12 math: 76 subtopics with CoT and tool-integrated solutions
Training details: 4K context packing, 500 steps, batch size 256, LR 5e-5
Results without tools: strong MATH performance vs larger open-source and many closed models
Results with tools: approaching 60% on MATH; competitiveness vs 10x larger models
Positioning among open and closed models (Qwen 72B, MetaMath 70B, WizardMath, GPT-4, Gemini)

outline.chapter_title: Reinforcement Learning for Alignment and Reasoning
outline.description: Provide background on PPO-style RL for LLM alignment, the role of reward models and KL control, and practical challenges in math reasoning.
subtopics: RLHF overview and the PPO actor-critic recipe
Reward models: outcome vs process supervision, training data construction
KL regularization: preventing reward overoptimization and mode collapse
Challenges for math RL: sparse rewards, long horizons, unstable critics, memory cost
Motivation for critic-free methods and group-based baselines

outline.chapter_title: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): An Efficient PPO Variant
outline.description: Dive into GRPO’s design: critic-free advantage estimation via group baselines, objective formulation, KL handling, and supervision modes.
subtopics: From PPO to GRPO: removing the value network and using group-average baselines
GRPO objective: clipped ratio term with per-token advantages
KL regularization as a direct divergence term with unbiased estimation
Outcome supervision: normalized end-of-output rewards as flat advantages
Process supervision: step-level rewards and token-level cumulative advantages
Algorithm anatomy: sampling G outputs per prompt, advantage computation, updates per batch
Iterative GRPO: refreshing reference policy and continuously training reward models with replay

outline.description: Detail the RL stage atop DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B, covering reward model training, GRPO settings, and in-domain vs out-of-domain gains.
subtopics: RL data: 144K CoT-format questions from GSM8K and MATH only
Reward model: trained from DeepSeekMath-Base 7B at LR 2e-5; dataset construction
GRPO hyperparameters: policy LR 1e-6, KL coeff 0.04, group size G=64, max length 1024, batch size 1024
Training protocol: single policy update after exploration per batch
In-domain gains: GSM8K 82.9% to 88.2%, MATH 46.8% to 51.7% (no tools, no voting)
Out-of-domain improvements: CMATH 84.6% to 88.8% despite no RL exposure
Self-consistency and robustness trends

outline.chapter_title: A Unified View of SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO
outline.description: Present a common gradient-based framework to compare methods by data source, reward function, and algorithmic gradient coefficients.
subtopics: Unified gradient form: data source, reward function, algorithm component
Offline vs online sampling: SFT/RFT/DPO vs Online RFT/PPO/GRPO
Rule-based vs model-based reward signals
Gradient coefficients: differential reinforcement and penalization
Conceptualizing all methods as direct or simplified RL
Practical mapping: how DPO and RFT relate to GRPO-style training

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Analyses: What Makes RL Work Better?
outline.description: Summarize ablations on data sourcing and algorithm design, and analyze why RL improves performance even with limited training data.
subtopics: Online vs offline training: Online RFT surpasses RFT later in training
GRPO vs Online RFT: advantages of magnitude-aware positive and negative updates
Process vs outcome supervision: fine-grained step rewards outperform outcome-only
Iterative RL: substantial gains in first iteration; benefits from refreshed reference and reward models
Why RL works: increases Maj@K but not Pass@K; promotes robust output distributions rather than core skill jumps
Misalignment in SFT distributions and preference alignment remedies

outline.chapter_title: Pretraining Insights: Code Helps, arXiv Less So
outline.description: Discuss ablation findings on code-first training, joint training mixes, catastrophic forgetting, and the limited value of arXiv-only corpora for math.
subtopics: Two-stage vs one-stage designs: code→math vs joint code+math
Program-aided solving boosts from code pretraining alone
Mitigating forgetting: mixing code and math in one-stage training
CoT without tools: code pretraining accelerates subsequent math learning
ArXiv-only corpora: little or negative impact across GSM8K, MATH, MMLU-STEM, miniF2F
Caveats: task specificity, combination effects, and scaling to larger models
Multilingual training: clear benefits for Chinese benchmarks

outline.chapter_title: Formal Mathematics and Tool-Aided Solving in Practice
outline.description: Provide practical workflows for tool-integrated math solving and formal proof generation used in DeepSeekMath evaluations.
subtopics: Python tool use: setting up math and sympy, sandboxing, capturing outputs
Prompt templates for PoT and tool-integrated reasoning
Isabelle environment: from informal statements to formal proofs
Proof sketches and Sledgehammer: filling proof gaps automatically
Reliability and verification: when to trust tool outputs
Common pitfalls in symbolic algebra and formal proof synthesis

outline.description: Critically examine known weaknesses, potential risks, and promising research directions identified by the DeepSeekMath project.
subtopics: Current gaps: geometry and theorem-proof areas vs closed models
Few-shot limitations at 7B scale compared to GPT-4
Data selection biases and their impact on topic coverage
Reward model robustness and label noise in process supervision datasets
Improving data sources: broader prompts and out-of-distribution questions
Advanced sampling and decoding: tree search methods for exploration
Efficient inference for scalable exploration (speculative decoding, etc.)
Weak-to-strong alignment and robustness to noisy rewards
Reward model generalization and calibrated uncertainty
Ethical considerations: data governance, contamination, and reproducibility

outline.chapter_title: Implementation Guide: Reproducing and Extending DeepSeekMath
outline.description: Offer a hands-on blueprint for engineers and researchers to replicate key components and extend the system to new domains.
subtopics: Data pipeline engineering: fastText training, domain mining, deduplication at scale
Decontamination recipes and validation
Pretraining setup: HAI-LLM framework, optimizer configs, batch sizing, context lengths
SFT pipeline: dataset curation, formatting CoT/PoT/tool traces, packing strategies
Reward model training: dataset creation, labeling strategies, replay buffers
GRPO training scripts: sampling groups, advantage normalization, KL tuning
Evaluation harness: deterministic decoding vs sampling, self-consistency, tool execution
Logging and diagnostics: reward distributions, KL tracking, gradient magnitudes
Compute and memory budgeting: avoiding critics, batching, and mixed precision

outline.description: Reinforce learning through practical assignments that mirror core components of the paper.
subtopics: Build and iterate a fastText-based domain classifier for a niche STEM field
Run a 1.3B pretraining comparison on two small math corpora
Construct a mini SFT dataset with CoT and PoT for algebra word problems
Implement outcome- and process-supervised reward models for a toy math set
Train a GRPO loop without a critic and compare to Online RFT
Measure Maj@K vs Pass@K before and after RL; interpret differences
Autoformalize simple problems into Isabelle and verify with Sledgehammer

outline.description: Summarize key terms and symbols used throughout the textbook and point to foundational and follow-up literature.
subtopics: Key terms: CoT, PoT, GRPO, PPO, KL regularization, self-consistency, Maj@K, Pass@K
Notation recap: policies, rewards, advantages, reference models
Core references: PPO, GAE, RLHF, process supervision, math LLM corpora
Suggested readings on formal methods, symbolic math, and decoding strategies
